Summary: For most of modern history, science assumed an eternal universe. The Big Bang reversed that: the universe is expanding from a beginning, and theorems like Borde-Guth-Vilenkin suggest any expanding universe must have a boundary in the past. A universe with a beginning points beyond itself to a Beginner.
KeyPoints: Expansion points back to a beginning; The Borde-Guth-Vilenkin theorem supports a past boundary; A beginning needs a cause
RelatedTopics: Creation; The Universe; Science and Faith
